title: Solara Reach — campaign raw jot
content:
Quick context: Solara Health is a regional telehealth operator (4 states) with a rapid roadmap to add automated triage and post-visit summarization. Heard via Tim (solutions) that their CTO is thinking about an on-prem-ish solution because of PHI concerns; they're open to a hybrid (private control plane + VPC-hosted runtime). This doc is raw — outreach drafts, priority contacts, objection rehearsals, and things to confirm before a pilot ask.

Top-line hypothesis about fit:
- Use-case: front-door symptom triage (asynchronous chat + structured form) + clinician summarization after visits + embeddings for knowledge retrieval of internal protocols and payer rules.
- Why Redwood: consistent low-latency inference for conversational triage, private deployment option for PHI, and cost controls via caching/batching that matter for high-volume chat.

People & signals (what I found quickly):
- CTO: Miguel Alvarez — LinkedIn mentions prior role at a large HMO, speaks frequently about security and SSO.
- Dir of Eng: Priya Nair — focused on infra and integrations. Has posts about moving from single-cloud to multi-region for resilience.
- Product lead: Hannah Ortiz — runs digital triage/UX. Looked at her slides from a webinar — they prototype with a generic intent engine today.
- Procurement/legal contact unknown yet — likely engaged once PHI questions surface.

Notes from Tim (internal slack):
- Solara currently uses a mix of hosted vendors for NLP (hospitality-grade chat vendors) and a growing amount of homegrown rules for escalation.
- Concern: hallucination risk for triage (clinicians can't have bogus suggestions).
- Constraint: must keep logs tenant-separated, ability to turn off persistence for certain flows.

Key positioning bullets (short for outreach):
- Production reliability: predictable latency for chatting at 30 RPS peak with autoscaling pools.
- PHI-safe deployments: private control plane + VPC-enabled runtime; KMS/HSM integrations for keys.
- Quality guardrails: eval-driven monitoring, prompt set regression alerts, and ability to pin model versions with canary rollouts.
- Cost predictability: dedicated capacity options + batching and KV-prefix caching to lower per-token spend.

Cold email draft (short):
Subject: Quick pilot idea for Solara’s triage — private LLM runs in your VPC
Hi Miguel — saw your notes about improving triage accuracy while keeping PHI inside your network. We’ve helped operators run LLM-based triage with a private Redwood runtime (VPC, KMS, no persistence option) and a short pilot that demonstrates safe non-hallucinating replies + summarization metrics. Can I book 20 minutes next week to outline a 4-week pilot and the data controls we’d need?
— Maya

Longer outreach / SDR sequence (3 steps):
1) Short email above + one-pager attachment (pilot skeleton) — wait 3 days.
2) Follow-up: value metrics (latency, cost per convo, reduction in triage-hand-offs in comparable customers), ask for intro to Priya or product.
3) Call/LinkedIn touch: leave a 30s video or quick screen snippet of a private demo (no Solara data) showing triage latency and fallback policy.

Phone / discovery script bullets:
- Opening: "We help healthcare platforms run private LLMs for triage and clinician notes with controls for PHI/retention."
- Quick fact-checks: "Do you run any LLM inference in your cloud today? How do you think about PHI for chat?"
- Risk probes: "What's the biggest operational worry — latency at scale, hallucinations, auditing, or procurement?"
- Pilot ask: "We can run a 4-week pilot in your staging VPC using pseudonymized logs — scope: 1) triage bot with strict templates + 2) summarization pipeline for 200 visits. Interested?"

Objection handling (expected):
- Objection: "We can't send PHI to an external API."
  Response: "Understood — our Private deployment runs in your VPC with a private control plane option. You can opt to never persist logs, and we integrate with your KMS/HSM for keys. Also we can sign BAAs and provide audit logs for every inference.
  Practical follow-up: offer a technical note showing network flow and data residency.

- Objection: "Hallucinations are unacceptable for triage."
  Response: "We build in deterministic guardrails: retrieval-augmented prompts with provenance citations, policy templates that constrain open-ended text, model pinning + canary rollouts and automated quality regression alerts tied to your prompt set. Pilot includes a small eval set (10–20 critical queries) to measure hallucination rate baseline vs. model tuning.

- Objection: "This will be expensive at scale."
  Response: "We can start with a dedicated pool sized for expected concurrency and show how KV prefix caching + batching reduces per-token cost substantially for repeated triage patterns. We’ll propose a cost-control playbook and report real token economics during the pilot.

Technical checklist to validate before pilot (dev questions for Priya / infra):
- VPC setup: do they allow peered network with vendor infra? If not, can we run a fully self-hosted runtime in their cloud account?
- KMS: which key provider (AWS KMS, Azure, HashiCorp)?
- Data retention: can they produce a pseudonymized dataset for eval or will we need synthetic?
- SSO & user mapping: who will administer the pilot (IAM access to our control plane or their tenant-admin)?
- Latency SLO: target 300–600 ms p95 for triage replies? (Confirm)

Pilot skeleton (4 weeks) — quick, low-friction:
Week 0: kickoff + infra checklist (VPC/KMS), agree success metrics + eval questions.
Week 1: deploy runtime (staging), small dataset ingest (protocol docs), configure retrieval store, run initial model + templates.
Week 2: integrate triage UI stub, run A/B internal tests vs current rules for 500 sessions, tune prompt templates.
Week 3: measure hallucination/regression metrics, run clinician review of 50 summaries, iterate.
Week 4: handoff findings, cost breakdown, decision workshop (move to prod / expand scope).

Metrics we'll show in pilot:
- p95 latency for reply
- hallucination incidence (binary) on the eval set
- % of sessions auto-resolved vs escalated to clinician
- per-conversation token cost and projected monthly spend at 10k convs/mo

Quick competitor notes (to prep legal):
- Vendor A: hosted-only, cheaper but no VPC option — risk for PHI.
- Vendor B: self-hosted open-source runtime but no dedicated ops/rollouts — more build for them.
- Redwood angle: middle ground — managed ops with private deployment options, rollouts, and quality monitoring baked in.

Open questions I want answered before formalizing pilot ask:
- Confirm the exact regulatory boundary they care about (HIPAA-compliant logging vs no-logging).
- Who owns procurement approvals and what procurement cadence looks like?
- Are there existing vendor relationships that block VPC peering?

Immediate next steps (owner = Maya):
- Send initial cold email to Miguel + attach a 1-pager pilot sketch (this week).
- Ask Tim for direct intro to Priya if Miguel doesn't respond within 72 hours.
- Draft a 2-page technical note on "Redwood Private for PHI-sensitive triage" for Priya/infra.
- Create a short internal playbook for SRE/solutions to estimate dedicated pool sizing for 1k, 5k, 10k conv/mo.

Scratch ideas for assets to attach:
- One-pager: pilot outline + three success metrics.
- Whitepaper: "Reducing hallucinations for clinical triage" (2–3 pages).
- Diagram: network flow for VPC + KMS (technical note).

Random jots / voice notes I might use in a call:
- "We treat model rollouts like code rollouts — canary small percent of traffic, automatic rollback on quality regression."
- "For triage we typically hard-limit free-form advice and rely on retrieval + templated outputs for action items."

Keep it rough — this is my outbound scratchpad. If Miguel answers, refine into a short one-pager and a concise tech appendix.

End of jot.
